title: Community B L1 · Duke Launch — Choose My Challenges
sub: Browse it · Pick it · Pledge it
learningObjective: To choose my Duke challenges for the year and complete my first mini-challenge.
successCriteria: I can say what the Duke award is and how evidence works.
I can choose three challenges that stretch me.
I can complete my first mini-challenge today.
scText: By the end you will have browsed the real challenge booklet, pledged your three challenges on a signed pledge card, and completed mini-challenge #1 — evidence photo and comment already in your log.
aspire1: pick at least one challenge that scares you a little bit.
aspire2: convince a partner to swap one easy pick for a braver one.

arrival.heading: Match the challenge to its family
arrival.tipWait: tell your partner one thing you have always wanted to learn to do.

items.n: Learn to use a plaster & bandage
Pack my own bag for the day

starter.heading: What can you already do that YOU taught yourself?
starter.prompt: With your partner: something you learned without school — a game skill, a recipe, a trick, fixing something. How did you learn it?
starter.stems:
“I taught myself to…”
“I learned it by…”
“It took me about…”
starter.hint: Games count. Phones count. Bikes count. Anything you got better at through practice counts.

iDo.heading: How the Duke award works
cards: Small real-life challenges: cookery, first aid, eco, independence. You pick them.
Every challenge = one photo + one comment in your log. That is the whole system.
Your tutor signs each challenge when the evidence is in. Signed set = award level.
Some challenges take more than one go. That is the design, not a failure.
iDo.miscWrong: “Awards are only for the clever kids.”
iDo.miscRight: The Duke award has no test and no grades. It is signed off on evidence of DOING — turning up and trying is literally the whole method.

weDo.heading: Sort the challenges into their families
weDo.hint: Ask: is it about food, the outdoors, helping someone hurt, or looking after yourself?

items.n: Put someone in the recovery position

practical.heading: Launch stations 🏅
practical.tip: three challenges — one that sounds fun, one that sounds useful, one that stretches you. All three, not three easy ones.
stations: Real challenge booklets on the table. Sticky-flag every challenge that interests you — no limit yet. Talk them over with a partner or TA.
Narrow your flags to THREE using the choosing rule. Write them on your pledge card, sign it, get your TA to countersign. This card goes on the Duke wall.
Do your first one right now: choose from — make squash safely for your table · pack a bag properly with the checklist · tie a secure knot/lace. Photo + one-line comment = evidence banked.

overlay: Pledge made, first challenge logged — your Duke year starts today.
taBriefs: Meet & greet. Booklets, sticky flags, pledge cards and mini-challenge kit laid out.
Arrival task: challenge sorting — if pupils debate categories, that IS the engagement. Steer, don't settle.
LO slide: read together. 'No test, no grades' is the hook for this cohort — say it plainly.
Starter: self-taught skills — this reframes every pupil as already a learner. Scribe examples.
I Do: the resilience card matters most here. Normalise multiple attempts out loud.
We Do: rotate tapping. The 999 script chip links to our safeguarding assembly work — acknowledge briefly if pupils mention it.
PRACTICAL: you run Pledge Cards — countersign only when the choosing rule is genuinely met; coach swaps warmly. Squash-making: cups and table mats, no kettles today.
Evidence: photograph every pledge card + mini-challenge. Scribe comments if needed, note 'TA scribed'. Cards go on the Duke wall before pupils leave.
Exit ticket: alone, one tap. Celebrate the braver picks by name.
